newsitem.title: HONDURAS: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

HONDURAS, Feb 11 - Puerto Cortes - Four vessels berthed of which 1 loading zinc concentrate, 3 discharging (1 paper in reels, 1 urea, 1 corn). 1 Vessel anchored, 1 in ballast. 12 Vessels due of which 5 to discharge/load containers/general cargo, 5 to load bananas, 2 passenger vessels, no berthing delays expected.

MEXICO, Feb 11 - All ports working normally. Tampico - Seven vessels in port of which 1 wood, 1 general cargo, 1 scrap, 2 minerals, 1 sugar, 1 corn. Altamira - Three vessels in port of which 2 chemicals, 1 butadiene. Veracruz - 13 Vessels in port of whh 3 containers, 2 general cargo, 1 sugar, 1 wood, 2 scrap, 3 grain, 1 anchored with cars. Manzanillo - Seven vessels in port of which 3 containers, 2 general cargo, 1 clinker, 1 with cars. Coatzacoalcos - Sixteen vessels in port of which 7 chemicals, 9 oil tankers.

PANAMA, Feb 10 - Balboa - One container, 1 passenger vessel. Cristobal - One bulker, 1 container vessel, 1 refrirator vessel. Panama Canal - Transit booking system working normally at full capacity. Position 10/2, 57 vessels due, 2 in queue, 13 booked, 44 due. 9/2, actual arrivals 34, transits 39, average of booked and non-booked canal waters time 21.6 hours.

UNITED STATES, Feb 10 - Jersey City, NJ, Perth Amboy, NJ, Cartaret, NJ - No vessels. Port Newark, NJ - Three vessels in port. Port Elizabeth, NJ - One vessel in port. Bayway, NJ - One vessel in port. All northern New Jersey ports working normally, with no congestion/delays. Baltimore, MD - Port working normally, 7 bulkers, 3 container vessels, 1 ro-ro, 2 auto vessels, 1 tanker, 3 general cargo vessels, 1 cable vessel on stand-by. 3 Vessels in repair yard, 5 bulkers awaiting berths of which 3 to discharge sugar, 1 to discharge ore, 1 under arrest. Both coal piers open, with no vessels due before 12/2.

Hampton Roads, VA - Six general cargo/container vessels berthed and operating, 4 bulkers berthed loading coal, 1 anchored waiting to load. 2 Bulkers loading fertiliser, 1 loading grain, 1 discharging pumice. 3 Vessels berthed and under repair. Honolulu, HI - Honolulu harbour - 1 Container vessel, 1 tanker, 1 tug, 4 tugs and barges berthed. Honolulu anchorage - 1 Bulk carrier. Barbers Point - 2 Barges, 1 bulk carrier berthed. Offport mooring - No vessels.

East coast - Baltimore, MD - No congestion expected at Dundalk terminal this week. Baltimore harbour - low ceiling. Elevators and coal operations working well with no delays. Consol coal - Average waiting time 3 days. Liquid bulk facilities working normally, no berthing congestion. Anchorages vacant at Baltimore and Annapolis. Charleston, SC - Container terminals - Light to moderate vessel traffic expected this week, but no delays expected. No delays at oil terminal or grain elevator. Jacksonvill FL - No heavy berthing congestion expected for Jacksonville and Fernandina Beach, FL.

New York, NY - No congestion at anchorages, none at container or tanker terminals. Sugar terminals congested. Norfolk, VA - Southern coal pier - 16 Vessels due this week, at present 3 vessels anchored waiting to load. Dominion terminal - 9 Vessels due. Pier IX coal terminal - 4 Vessels due during the week. Cargill - No vessels due. Container and general terminals working normally with no delays. Oil and bulker terminals working normally. All channels ice free with prevailing depths available. Southern coal pier will undertake scheduled maintenance to no. 1 ship loading system from April 8-29.

During this period, no. 1 ship loading system will be out of service. Philadelphia, PA - No congestion at Philadelphia, Camden or Wilmington. No dredging/navigational problems. Savannah, GA - Garden City terminals forecast busy week, with heaviest congestion during the first part of the week. Ocean termals forecast moderate congestion throughout the week. East coast terminal - Forecasting a busy week but no delays expected. Colonial Marine terminals bulk clay facility - Long delays expected. All liquid bulk facilities working normally with no congestion expected. Navigational normal. Vessels may expect delays due to seasonal fog.

Gulf coast - Houston, TX - Houston ship channel traffic back to normal. No congestion at Houston city docks, public elevator and Cargill elevator. However, congestion exists in some oil/chemical docks. New Orleans, LA - Grain shipments normal for the season. River stage at 10.6 feet and expected to go up to 11.2 feet by 12/2. Normal transit times expected. Bar pilots advise that the draft for the Mississippi river gulf outlet will be 36 feet. Present max. permissible draft at S.W. Pass is 47 feet fresh water for vessels under 100,000 dwt. And 46 feet fresh water for vessels over 100,000 dwt.

WEST COAST - Columbia river - Grain/bulk activity increasing significantly in Feb, March. Heavy congestion expected at all Columbia river elevators beginning 10/2 and throughout the month. Average waiting period 5 days. Coos Bay, OR - Port busy this week. Three wood-chip, 2 lumber, 1 log vessel loading. At present 1 log vessel is loading at Coos Bay dock and 1 vessel due for Dolphin terminal next week. Glenbrook nickel terminal expecting 2 more vessels in Feb. Vessel traffic expected to remain moderately busy for the remainder of the month. No vessel delays due to bad weather.

Long Beach, CA - Metropolitan (LB-212-214)- Moderately busy for Feb, with 1-2 days waiting at anchor expected. Koch Carbon (LB-211)- 4 Vessels due for Feb, no delays expected. Kaiser (LA-49) - Moderately busy for Feb, (coal,petcoke) 2-3 days berthing delay expected. Feb looks moderately busy in Los Angeles, Long Beach for bulk cargoes. Problems at Hugo-Neu scrape facility appear to have been settled. Seattle, WA - Both grain eletors have a backlog of vessels at anchor awaiting berth. Tacoma to remove drawbridge at the mouth of Blair waterway in the spring of 1997, providing significant improvements in safety and a reduction in transit restrictions and costs for large vessels utilising the waterway. Depth of water will be increased to 40 ft. Mllw and channel width will also be increased.
